relevance_note: The paper reports one identifiable child with a TNFAIP3 variant, Patient #18, who had 'a heterozygous c.259C>T mutation in TNFAIP3, indicating an A20 deficiency' (printed in the paper as 'Genetic analysis revealed a heterozygous c.259C>T mutation in TNFAIP3, indicating an A20 deficiency.').
method_note: Single-paper cohort of 24 children with primary immunodeficiencies; only Patient #18 carries a TNFAIP3 variant, so only this person is in scope (the other 23 patients have variants in other genes or no variant, and no relative of Patient #18 is described). Tables 1 and 4 are group-level counts and were not used for individual values. Patient #18 appears once in the text as 'Patient #18' and once in Table 2 as '#18'; the text form 'Patient #18' was used as the label. Age at diagnosis is the Table 2 cell '192/M'; the table legend defines 'A: age at the time of diagnosis (months)', so the value is given as '192 months' (ISO P192M) with the cell quoted as span. The '-' cells in the Physical findings and Additional manifestations columns of Table 2 are not defined as absent/negative anywhere in the legend, so they were treated as not reported. The paper prints no variant class, pathogenicity, ACMG criteria, functional assay, transcript, protein or genomic description for c.259C>T, and no parental testing, so those fields are not reported. is_proband is false with span null because no span can support a negative. Uncertainty: Table 2 lists 'LNH' (lymphonodular hyperplasia) as a histopathological finding; it was recorded in phenotypic_features but the checklist item 'lymphoproliferation or lymphadenopathy' was left not reported, because the paper never uses those words for this patient.
